prompt: The film is awful, but he stays because he already paid for the ticket.
why: The money is gone either way. Staying because of it is the sunk cost trap.
trap: Goals matter, but the trap is past spending.

prompt: 'We've spent two years on it, we can't stop now,' though it clearly won't work.
why: Past effort doesn't make future effort worth it.
trap: Ignoring disproof is related, but the pull is past investment.

prompt: She keeps fixing the old car because she already put so much into it.
tells: already put so much into it
why: Decide on future costs, not past ones.
trap: It isn't base rates; it's past spending.

prompt: He eats until he feels sick because the buffet cost a lot.
tells: because the buffet cost a lot
why: The cost is paid. Eating more doesn't get it back.
trap: There's a side effect, but the cause is sunk cost.

prompt: A new manager asks, 'If we were starting today, would we choose this?'
why: Ignoring what's already spent escapes the sunk cost trap.
trap: It defines a goal, but the clue is starting fresh.

prompt: She keeps going to a course she hates because she paid for the whole year.
tells: she paid for the whole year
why: The fee is spent; only future value matters.
trap: It's about the past payment, not later effects.
